item.title: Safe Vancouver Bicycle crossings August 2026 update
item.description:
East / West

  • Cross Kingsway at Miller (e.g. if you are going to Shiok or 88)
  • Cross Nanaimo at 24th / Vanness (e.g. if you are going to Pampanga’s at Joyce)
  • Cross Victoria at 19th (new in 2023 beg button/flashing lights)
  • Cross Commercial Drive (just before it turns into Victoria Diversion) at 18th
  • Cross Nanaimo at 20th
  • No beg buttons on Kaslo at 1st, Broadway and 12th
  • Cross Knight at 47th
  • Cross Knight at 37th
  • Cross Knight at 19th
  • Cross Main at 18th
  • Cross Main at 14th
  • Cross Fraser at 19th
  • Cross Fraser at 27th
  • Cross Fraser at 28th (29th Avenue Bikeway)
  • Cross Cambie at 14th
  • Cross Cambie at 18th
  • Cross Cambie at 20th
  • Cross Victoria at 22nd (no safe crossing at Stainsbury or Porter)

North / South

  • Unsafe at rush hour and weekdays since there is no light! –> Cross King Edward at Nanton (use Arbutus Greenway at busy times)
  • Cross Hastings at Lakewood
  • Cross Hastings at Templeton
  • Cross Hastings at Kamloops
  • Cross 1st at Lillooet
  • Cross 1st at Slocan
  • Cross 12th at Heather
  • Cross Broadway at Slocan
  • Cross 12th at Slocan
  • Cross Kingsway at Glen
  • Cross Kingsway at Miller
  • Cross Kingsway at Windsor
  • Cross 22nd at Slocan (new crossing that was built in 2025 or 2024!)
  • Cross 49th at Cypress
  • Cross 49th at Tisdall (not Heather or Willow)
  • Cross 41st at Angus
  • Cross 29th at Atlin
  • No safe crossing at Skeena and 1st Avenue (just walk)

item.description:
Discovered: Aug 16, 2026 16:33 (UTC) ME:: tl-dr-ing; Transactional web of ‘AI’ and human web ; Andy Budd:: Will AI Agents Kill the Web as We Know It?

QUOTE

  • Read the whole thing: Andy Budd:: Will AI Agents Kill the Web as We Know It?

One layer will be invisible: efficient, transactional, built for machines—powered by protocols like MCP. The other will be human-facing: emotional, experiential, and deeply brand-driven.

AI agents won’t kill the web. But they will radically reshape it. And just like with retail, the winners will be the ones who make that second layer worth visiting.

item.title: Must try this new app from Marco Arment:: Unforgetful
item.description:
Discovered: Aug 16, 2026 16:29 (UTC) Must try this new app from Marco Arment:: Unforgetful

QUOTE:

  • Read the whole thing: Marco Arment:: Unforgetful
  • It’s impossible to lose a task. Notifications always repeat, even if you miss or dismiss them, until the task is completed or deleted.
  • Designed for procrastination. Snoozing is a core feature, with thoughtful intervals that scale as you snooze a task more.
  • Nothing is hidden away. A hidden task is a forgotten task. No folders, no tags, no organization, no different views or modes.
  • No judgment or shame. Nothing is overdue. You’re not in trouble. Everything is either due now or in the future. Didn’t get to it today? Maybe tomorrow. Every day is a fresh start.

item.description:
Discovered: Aug 15, 2026 15:15 (UTC) ME:: tl-dr-ing The hypocrisy of the dominant hegemony means it’s OK to moan about cancellation, harmless pronouns and loss of prestige for public figures and also it’s OK to not hold people accountable for imprisoning dissidents, dismantling public education and eroding democracy; Jamelle Bouie via Kottke:: The Moral Unseriousness of Centrist & Conservative Pundits

  • Oh and BTW BLM = Good; J6 = Bad (and the perpetrators including Дональд Трамп should be in prison like anybody who else breaks the law)

QUOTE

  • Watch the whole 10 minute Jamelle Bouie video: The pundits have completely lost the plot

  • Michael Hobbes has been talking about this on Bluesky as well:

Centrists convinced themselves annoying leftists on twitter were an equivalent threat to Jan 6 insurrectionists. They wildly inflated the threat of left-wing authoritarianism while ignoring how it was taking hold on the right.

Meanwhile, the right never meant any of it. They moaned about “cancellation” for a decade but embarked on mass firings as soon as they took power. They pretended to care about “free speech restrictions” and “educational indoctrination” while embarking on them every chance they got.

The excesses of the Woke 1 era mostly amount to cringe public statements, harmless vocabulary updates and loss of prestige for public figures.

The backlash to Woke 1, on the other hand, is imprisoning dissidents, dismantling public education and eroding democracy. That’s what needs reckoning
